title: reflect
body:
## reflect

Mirrors the input across an axis-aligned plane and outputs an unstructured grid (a composite input gives a multiblock of unstructured grids) holding the mirrored copy, plus the original when copyInput is true. Use it to rebuild a full model from a half- or quarter-symmetry simulation, or to mirror a part for display. The plane is x, y or z = centre (Schemaxis default plane X at 0) or one face of the input's bounding box (X Min to Z Max). Vector and tensor arrays such as velocity are mirrored with the geometry because ParaView's FlipAllInputArrays stays at its default (on); scalars are copied unchanged.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The two halves are appended, not merged: points on the mirror plane are duplicated and the halves are not connected. Run cleanGrid afterwards when connectivity matters, e.g. before surface, connectivity or point-based gradients.
- Image data, rectilinear and structured grids become an unstructured grid, which can need much more memory than the input.
- Schemaxis's serial native acceptance run (examples/schemaxis/extended-coverage.json) executes this operation once, on a sphere with the default options; it does not check this operation's output values, so inspect the result on your own data.

Native constructor: `Reflect`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plane` | The value of this property determines which plane to reflect across. If the value is X, Y, or Z, the value of the Center property determines where the plane is placed along the specified axis. The other six options (X Min, X Max, etc.) place the reflection plane at the specified face of the bounding box of the input dataset. | `{"type":"enum","values":["X Min","Y Min","Z Min","X Max","Y Max","Z Max","X","Y","Z"]}` | `"X"` | `"X"` |
| `centre` | If the value of the Plane property is X, Y, or Z, then the value of this property specifies the center of the reflection plane. | `{"type":"number"}` | `0` | `0` |
| `copyInput` | When true, the output contains the original input plus its mirror image, e.g. the full model rebuilt from a half-model; when false, only the mirrored copy is returned. The two parts are not merged at the mirror plane. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` | `true` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "reflect",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  }
}
```
